title: Underlying coherent localization of a dg model enhancement
statement:
Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], coherent functors and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and derived chain enrichment and enriched localization of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Work in fixed universes large enough for the categories below. Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups. Locally presentable means that for some infinite regular cardinal it is generated under the corresponding filtered colimits by a small family of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve those colimits. The enriched Hom complexes have unital associative chain-map compositions and the ordinary morphisms as their degree-zero cycles. Tensors and cotensors satisfy the natural complex adjunctions $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(K\otimes A,B)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,B))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,B^K)$. Suppose retract-closed classes $C,F,W$ satisfy two-out-of-three for $W$, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are functorial weak factorization systems generated by sets: every map factors into the two indicated classes, and those classes are exactly each other's diagonal-lifting classes. Assume that for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$ the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,X)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,Y)$$
is degreewise surjective, and is a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ lies in $W$. Let $\ell:\mathcal M\to\mathcal D$ be its enriched localization at $W$, and let $U\mathcal D$ have mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathbf Z[0],\mathcal D(x,y))$.

The induced functor $q:N(\mathcal M)\to U\mathcal D$ is a universal homotopy coherent localization of the ordinary nerve at $W$. Precisely, for every infinity category $\mathcal E$, precomposition induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}(U\mathcal D,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{W}(N(\mathcal M),\mathcal E),$$
where the right side is the full subcategory of functors sending the arrows of $W$ to equivalences. This equivalence includes all coherent natural transformations and their higher homotopies.

source.place: Agent-supplied dg-model comparison needed before the paragraph-2 mapping-complex calculation. No Stacks tag states this enriched/ordinary comparison. WANTED: an archived general dg-model localization reference; compare Lurie, Higher Algebra (2017), Remark 1.3.1.12, Proposition 1.3.1.17 and the chain-complex example Proposition 1.3.4.5, with cosimplicial-frame mapping spaces. The stated generalization is agent-formulated, not claimed verbatim from those propositions.

proof.text: Put $C_n=N\mathbf Z[\Delta^n]$, with a nondegenerate simplex $[i_0<\cdots<i_r]$ in cochain degree $-r$ and differential its alternating boundary. A monotone map sends this generator to its image simplex if the image vertices are distinct, and to zero otherwise. These formulas give a cosimplicial complex $C_\bullet$. Its augmentation $\varepsilon_n:C_n\to\mathbf Z[0]$ sends each vertex to $1$ and positive-dimensional simplices to zero. On the augmented complex, inserting the initial vertex $0$ when it is absent, and giving zero when it is present, is the usual contraction: $dh+hd=1-v_0\varepsilon_n$. Thus each augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The latching complex is the subcomplex spanned by proper faces, since its basis is precisely the simplices contained in proper faces and the overlap relations identify equal basis simplices. For $n>0$ its inclusion into $C_n$ attaches just the top generator in degree $-n$ with its prescribed alternating boundary, hence is a pushout of $S^{-n+1}\hookrightarrow D^{-n}$ of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. For $n=0$ it is $0\to\mathbf Z[0]$, a cofibration by the cofibrant-unit clause of that node. Consequently $C_\bullet$ is a cosimplicial frame on $\mathbf Z[0]$ in the projective model category of complexes, with degree-zero augmentation the identity, in the terminology of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping].

source.place: Agent construction for paragraph 2: normalized simplex chains, their contraction and latching cells; compare Hovey Definition 5.2.7 and HA Remark 1.3.1.12.

proof.text: Fix a cofibrant $P\in\mathcal M$. The initial object is also terminal: enrichment makes the category preadditive, and the identity of the initial object is zero, so every map into it is zero. Denote it by $0$. The tensor adjunction identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,0)$ with the zero complex, since maps from every complex $K$ into it correspond to maps $K\otimes P\to0$, of which there is exactly one. The cotensor adjunction likewise identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(0,X)$ with the zero complex for every $X$: maps from $K$ into this complex correspond to maps $0\to X^K$, of which there is exactly one. Thus both $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(0,X)$ and $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(0,Y)$ in the mapping axiom vanish. Applying the assumed mapping axiom to $0\to P$ and a fibration $X\to Y$ shows that $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,X)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Y)$ is degreewise surjective, and a quasi-isomorphism if the fibration is trivial. The ordinary tensor--Hom adjunction therefore makes $T_P(K)=K\otimes P$ a left Quillen functor from the projective complex model of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]: transposing a lifting problem against a (trivial) fibration gives a lift against its image under the right adjoint. This proves preservation of both cofibrations and trivial cofibrations using the two characterized lifting classes. By [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], $T_PC_\bullet$ is a cosimplicial frame on $P$. In particular all $C_n\otimes P\to P$ are weak equivalences; no claim that arbitrary tensor inputs preserve weak equivalences is needed.

source.place: Agent argument for paragraph 2: deriving the chain tensor from the stated mapping axiom and transporting the explicit frame.

proof.text:
Let $q_0:N\mathcal M\to\mathcal L$ be the universal ordinary infinity localization supplied by [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]; the model weak equivalences form a wide subcategory because identities are in both lifting classes and two-out-of-three gives closure under composition. For cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $I$, apply [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] to the frame of step 2. Apply that same node to the frame $C_\bullet$ of step 1 and the fibrant complex $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,I)$; every complex is fibrant by [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. The latter node identifies the coherent monoidal localization of the complex model with $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, with unit $\mathbf Z[0]$. The tensor--Hom adjunction is an equality of the following simplicial mapping constructions, natural for every monotone simplex operator, not only on components:
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(q_0P,q_0I)\simeq\bigl[n\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C_n\otimes P,I)\bigr]\cong\bigl[n\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(C_n,H)\bigr]\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathbf Z[0],H).$$
Both displayed simplicial sets are Kan by the cited frame theorem. This identifies all mapping-space homotopy groups without any boundedness assumption on $H$.

source.place: Agent mapping-space calculation for paragraph 2: apply the same frame theorem in M and in unbounded complexes; Hovey Section 5.4 and the existing coherent frame comparison.

proof.text: The functor $q=U\ell$ inverts $W$ by [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. The universal property of $q_0$ in [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] therefore gives a coherent functor $F:\mathcal L\to U\mathcal D$ and a specified equivalence $Fq_0\simeq q$. By [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison], for the mixed pair $(P,I)$ the mapping object of $\mathcal D$ is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,I)$, naturally on the mixed domain. Under this identification, the map on spaces induced by $F$ is the comparison of step 3. To check the actual map, an $n$-simplex on its middle left is an evaluation map $a:C_n\otimes P\to I$. Its localization is the span $qP\xleftarrow{q\varepsilon_n}q(C_n\otimes P)\xrightarrow{qa}qI$, with an invertible left edge. A simplex operator is carried to the commuting square obtained by precomposition with $C_m\to C_n$, so these spans and their face/degeneracy compatibilities form the coherent evaluation comparison used by the frame theorem. On the chain-enriched side the same $a$ is its tensor adjoint $C_n\to H$. To see explicitly why evaluation gives that span without assuming that $\ell$ preserves arbitrary tensors, let $b_n:C_n\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,C_n\otimes P)$ be the tensor coevaluation. Compose it with the map on enriched Homs induced by $\ell$. Postcomposition with $q\varepsilon_n$ takes this map to $\varepsilon_n$ times $1_{qP}$: before localization this is exactly the naturality identity of the tensor adjunction, and an enriched functor preserves it. Postcomposition with the equivalence $q\varepsilon_n$ is an equivalence on derived mapping objects, so the image of $b_n$ is its inverse applied to $\varepsilon_n1_{qP}$. Composing with $qa$ now identifies the localized adjoint $C_n\to\mathcal D(qP,qI)$ with $qa\,(q\varepsilon_n)^{-1}\varepsilon_n$, exactly the evaluation span above. The augmentations $\varepsilon_n:C_n\to\mathbf Z[0]$ form an objectwise equivalence of the whole cosimplicial diagram in derived complexes. Likewise step 2 makes $q(C_\bullet\otimes P)\to\operatorname{const}(qP)$ objectwise an equivalence. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes these transformations coherent natural equivalences and supplies inverse coherent diagrams. The preceding identities are coherent in that diagram and in the parameter $a$: they come from tensor-adjunction naturality and preservation of composition by the enriched functor, before passing to homotopy classes. In the frame constructions of step 3, this identifies the parameterized evaluation comparison on each simplex and all its restriction maps. Inverting the augmentation here retains this entire coherent family, including the homotopies carried by its positive-dimensional simplices. Postcomposition with $q\varepsilon_n$ has a homotopy inverse given by composition with an inverse edge; its two inverse homotopies follow from the inverse equations and associativity. Applying that inverse to the coherent coevaluation identity therefore identifies the induced mapping-space map with the comparison of step 3. Consequently the map induced by $F$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every cofibrant-source, fibrant-target pair. This is a comparison of the specified functor, rather than an abstract equality of homotopy groups.

source.place: Agent compatibility check for paragraph 2: the evaluation spans underlying both frame comparisons and the specified localization functor.

proof.text: Factor $0\to X$ and $Y\to0$ to obtain a cofibrant replacement $QX\to X$ and a fibrant replacement $Y\to TY$. Their maps lie in $W$, so they give equivalences under both $q_0$ and $q$. Conjugating the mapping-space map of $F$ by these equivalences identifies it with the map for $(QX,TY)$ proved to be an equivalence in step 4. Every object of $\mathcal L$ is represented by an object of $\mathcal M$, since the hammock construction and its locally Kan replacement retain the objects by [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. Hence $F$ is fully faithful on all objects. Every object of $\mathcal D$ is equivalent to the image of a bifibrant object by the full-bifibrant-presentation clause of [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison]. Its underlying equivalence is also an equivalence in $U\mathcal D$. Thus $F$ is essentially surjective.

source.place: Agent reduction to mixed replacements and essential surjectivity for paragraph 2.

proof.text: Here is a coherent inverse, so no inference from equivalence of ordinary homotopy categories is being used. For every $d\in U\mathcal D$, choose $x_d\in\mathcal L$ and an equivalence $u_d:d\to Fx_d$ using step 5. Full faithfulness says that $v\mapsto F(v)u_d$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(x_d,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{U\mathcal D}(d,Fz)$ for every $z$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] to $F$. It constructs a coherent left adjoint $G$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$ and their triangle homotopies. The universal arrow $(Gd,\eta_d)$ is equivalent to $(x_d,u_d)$: under the two representing equivalences the identities give mutually inverse maps, since their composites correspond to the respective identities. It follows that every $\eta_d$ is an equivalence. The triangle identity $F\epsilon\circ\eta F\simeq1$ makes each $F\epsilon_x$ an equivalence. A fully faithful functor reflects equivalences: lift an inverse class through the equivalence of mapping spaces and use injectivity on components to get the two inverse equations. Hence every $\epsilon_x$ is an equivalence. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] now makes $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ coherent natural equivalences. Therefore $F$ is an equivalence of infinity categories.

source.place: Agent construction of a coherent inverse from the verified mapping-space comparison; generic local-adjoint tool, without replacing the coefficient unit route.

proof.text:
For any infinity category $\mathcal E$, restriction along the equivalence $F$ has inverse restriction along $G$; the natural equivalences are given by precomposing with the unit and counit of step 6. Composing it with restriction along $q_0$ gives
$$\operatorname{Fun}(U\mathcal D,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_W(N\mathcal M,\mathcal E),$$
where the second equivalence is precisely [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. Since $Fq_0\simeq q$, this composite is restriction along the specified $q$. Precomposition and its inverse act on whole coherent functor categories, so the conclusion includes coherent natural transformations and their higher homotopies.

source.place: Agent conclusion for paragraph 2: transport the full functor-category universal property along the constructed equivalence.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q56-351e64495 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 proof-dependency and 3 statement-dependency statements, unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general and paragraph 2 of the main-20261015 prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof. The statement is true and unchanged: the dg analogue of HA 1.3.1.17, with hypotheses identical to dg-model-mapping-comparison. Step 1: I checked the normalized-chain frame myself. The contraction satisfies dh+hd=1-v0·ε. The latching object is N Z[∂Δ^n], and for n>0 the latching map is the pushout of S^{-n+1}→D^{-n}. For n=0 the map 0→Z[0] is a cofibration by the cofibrant-unit clause. Step 2: the initial object is a zero object by preadditivity, and Hom(P,0)=0=Hom(0,X). The axiom applied to 0→P makes Hom(P,-) right Quillen, so the frame node's left-adjoint clause applies as stated. Step 3: the Z^0 tensor-Hom adjunction is natural in C_n, so it identifies the whole simplicial sets; every complex is fibrant. Step 4 (3316 characters, long-step check): I verified the coevaluation identity myself: ℓ(b_n)=(qε_n)^{-1}_*(ε_n·1), so the localized adjoint of a is the evaluation span. This is one coherent naturality calculation with all non-elementary inputs cited, not a hidden lemma, so it stays as one step. Steps 5-7: mixed replacements, bifibrant essential surjectivity, the local-adjoint criterion, reflection of equivalences by a fully faithful functor and the componentwise criterion are all correct. No new nodes. The rg duplicate search over the dg-model and localization nodes found nothing. The BFS found no cycle. No SGA source is cited. The tool_use lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus (unit sk-prop-sf-cbc, a generic componentwise-equivalence criterion) is declared and accepted. No fixes.
